q-35257.name: Question 1
q-35257.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -6\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=5{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}=-2{b}_{1}?$
q-35257.worked_solution:
Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -6\end{aligned}]$, we can write $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =3{b}_{1}-6{b}_{2} \\  & =-6{b}_{2}+3{b}_{1} \\  & =-\frac{6}{5}(5{b}_{2})-\frac{3}{2}(-2{b}_{1}) \\  & =-\frac{6}{5}{c}_{1}-\frac{3}{2}{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{6}{5} \\ -\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}].$

a
[x]C=[3235]
b
[x]C=[−52−3]
c
[x]C=[2−32]
d
[x]C=[−1−4]
e
[x]C=[−65−32]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since [x]B=[3−6], we can write x as follows:

x=3b1−6b2=−6b2+3b1=−65(5b2)−32(−2b1)=−65c1−32c2

Therefore, [x]C=[−65−32].

q-112862.name: Question 4
q-112862.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=2{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}={b}_{1}+{b}_{2}?$
q-112862.worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}=2{b}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}={b}_{1}+{b}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $b$'s in terms of $c$'s. From the first equation, we get 

$$
{b}_{2}=\frac{1}{2}{c}_{1}.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation, we obtain

$$
{c}_{2}={b}_{1}+(\frac{1}{2}{c}_{1})\,⟹\,{b}_{1}=-\frac{1}{2}{c}_{1}+{c}_{2}.
$$

 

Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]$, we can write the vector $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={b}_{1}-5{b}_{2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}{c}_{1}+{c}_{2}-5(\frac{1}{2}{c}_{1}) \\  & =-\frac{6}{2}{c}_{1}+{c}_{2} \\  & =-3{c}_{1}+{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

EXPLANATION

We are given that

{c1=2b2c2=b1+b2.

First, we express the b's in terms of c's. From the first equation, we get

b2=12c1.

Substituting this into the second equation, we obtain

c2=b1+(12c1)⟹b1=−12c1+c2.

Since [x]B=[1−5], we can write the vector x as follows:

x=b1−5b2=−12c1+c2−5(12c1)=−62c1+c2=−3c1+c2

Therefore, [x]C=[−31].

q-113070.name: Question 5
q-113070.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=2{b}_{1}+{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}=-{b}_{1}?$
q-113070.worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}=2{b}_{1}+{b}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}=-{b}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $b$'s in terms of $c$'s. From the second equation, we get 

$$
{b}_{1}=-{c}_{2}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{c}_{1}=2(-{c}_{2})+{b}_{2}\,⟹\,{b}_{2}={c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}.
$$

Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$, we can write the vector $x$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-{b}_{1}+3{b}_{2} \\  & =-(-{c}_{2})+3({c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}) \\  & ={c}_{2}+3{c}_{1}+6{c}_{2} \\  & =7{c}_{2}+3{c}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 7\end{aligned}].$

Let B={b1,b2} be a basis of R2 and [x]B=[−13]. What are the coordinates of x relative to the basis C={c1,c2}, where c1=2b1+b2 and c2=−b1?

a
[x]C=[−35]
b
[x]C=[37]
c
[x]C=[−53]
d
[x]C=[7−3]
e
[x]C=[73]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We are given that

{c1=2b1+b2c2=−b1.

First, we express the b's in terms of c's. From the second equation, we get

b1=−c2.

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

c1=2(−c2)+b2⟹b2=c1+2c2.

Since [x]B=[−13], we can write the vector x as follows:

x=−b1+3b2=−(−c2)+3(c1+2c2)=c2+3c1+6c2=7c2+3c1

Therefore, [x]C=[37].
